text:
Maya (PM): Quick sync — after GA we saw intermittent p99 spikes for short-chat sessions (~5% of requests). Some customers are asking for session persistence/stickiness. Need to decide: ship a small hotpatch to stabilize p99 or invest in the larger session-stickiness enhancement for the next minor release? Thoughts?

Logan (Eng Lead): I reproduced — spikes correlate with KV cache thrash when many short-lived sessions spawn. Low-hanging fix: tighten eviction heuristics and cap per-session open streams. Small diff, low risk.

Priya (SRE): If we push an eviction tweak it must be canaryed. Recommend 10% canary, monitor p99, mem, and error-rate dashboards. Gate behind a feature flag.

Sam (QA): Small patch → we can QA in ~48 hrs. Test matrix: session churn, reconnects, mem leak scan, perf harness regression. Need clear acceptance criteria.

Taylor (SE): The session-stickiness feature (persist session_id + KV reuse across reconnects) is what customers want long-term. That’s a product change (API + migration) — not a hotpatch. Sells well to enterprise but needs spec and security review.

Maya (PM): Proposal: two-track plan — 1) Immediate stabilization patch (P1) with eviction tweak + cap + FF + 10% canary, target rollout within 48h. 2) Parallel: spec & design for session-stickiness as an enhancement for next minor (v0.2). Owners: Logan for the patch; Taylor + Maya for the spec. Any objections?

Jamie (CS): Sounds good. Acme Corp reported the issue and is OK with a short-term patch while we work on the sticky session spec. I’ll keep them updated and capture the enterprise requirements.

Logan (Eng Lead): I'll open a PR for the eviction tweak and the per-session stream cap, link load tests and a reproducer, and include a simple FF. Will reference issue #4321. Sample deploy command in PR description:

```
# enable canary feature flag (ops)
redwood feature enable session-eviction-tweak --canary 10%
```

Maya (PM): Patch acceptance criteria (for the hotpatch):
- p99 returns to baseline (no >200ms increase over baseline)
- memory increase <5% under the same load profile
- no new error regressions (errors <= current baseline)
If any of these fail post-canary, we rollback.

Priya (SRE): I'll create the canary dashboard and a rollback alert: trigger if p99 > target OR error rate > 0.5% absolute. I’ll also add a short runbook entry for the patch rollout and rollback steps.

Sam (QA): Scheduling QA window now and will add two automated e2e cases to the perf harness (session churn and reconnect reuse). ETA: 36h for QA sign-off once PR is ready.

Taylor (SE): For the session-stickiness spec draft I propose: API header `X-Session-Id`, ability to opt-in per-route, server-side TTL controls, and a migration plan for clients that don’t send session ids. I’ll sketch and post a doc by EOD Friday.

Maya (PM): Great — I'll update the roadmap (move sticky-session to "next minor" and add the hotpatch to the immediate "stability" bucket). I’ll send a short update to #product and tag stakeholders when PR and spec links are live.

deploy-bot: deploy queued — canary 10% once PR merged and FF enabled.

Logan (Eng Lead): Opening the issue + PR now: https://redwood.internal/issue/4321 (PR will include links to perf runs). I’ll call out owner for rollback.

Jamie (CS): I’ll notify Acme and ask for permission to include them in the canary cohort if they want earlier verification.

Maya (PM): Thanks all. Running checklist: Logan (patch + PR), Priya (dashboards/alert), Sam (QA), Taylor (spec), Jamie (customer comms). Follow-up sync in #product once PR is merged. :thumbsup:
